research.title: Evidence Sensitivity in Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering
bullets: Designed supervisor-guided experiments comparing answer generation under relevant, distracting, and contradictory retrieved passages while holding questions and generation settings constant.
Evaluated answer correctness and evidence attribution, categorizing failures involving unsupported claims, conflicting passages, and excessive reliance on lexical overlap.

research.title: Lexical Shortcut Reliance in Natural Language Inference
bullets: Designed experiments with supervisor guidance to examine lexical overlap shortcuts in sentence-pair classification using controlled substitutions and label-preserving paraphrases.
Compared classifier behavior across original and perturbed examples, inspecting prediction changes and annotation ambiguity to distinguish shortcut reliance from semantic sensitivity.

publications.title: Examining Lexical Shortcut Reliance in Natural Language Inference Through Controlled Sentence Perturbations

work.title: Inventory and Order Documentation Support
bullets: Maintained inventory records, checked incoming deliveries against packing lists, and flagged discrepancies for review by the responsible operations staff.
Organized order paperwork, updated shipment status logs, and coordinated routine handoffs between receiving and dispatch staff during daily operations.

projects.title: Comparative Evaluation of Sparse and Dense Passage Retrieval
bullets: Implemented probabilistic sparse and pretrained dense retrieval baselines for document question answering, using consistent passage segmentation and shared evaluation queries.
Compared retrieval rankings using relevance judgments and inspected errors associated with rare terminology, paraphrased questions, and passages containing competing entities.

projects.title: Sequence Labeling Approaches for Named Entity Recognition
bullets: Implemented token classification baselines using a linear classifier and a fine-tuned transformer, aligning entity labels consistently across tokenization schemes.
Compared entity-level precision and recall across label categories, examining boundary errors, ambiguous mentions, and differences between frequent and uncommon entities.
